initial_observation.demographics: A 41-year-old man without prior vaccination of COVID-19
initial_observation.encounter_context: presented to medical care with symptoms
initial_observation.chief_complaint: worsening headache accompanied by nausea and photophobia for 3 days
initial_observation.first_contact_summary: He was alert with normal vital signs, no signs of meningeal irritation or neurological symptoms, blood tests and head CT were unremarkable

evidence_items.source_text: On physical examination, he was alert, with a temperature of 36.7℃, blood pressure of 105/60 mm Hg, pulse rate of 70/min, respiration rate of 16/min and oxygen saturation at 97% in ambient air. No signs of meningeal irritation or neurological symptoms were observed.

He wore a mask as a precaution for COVID-19. On removing the mask, rashes with blisters were observed on the left side of his nose and hard palate in the area of the second branch of the trigeminal nerve (figures 1 and 2). The patient experienced skin rashes and oral cavity dysesthesia before his visit, but believed them to be unrelated to the headache.
The rapid test was positive for varicella zoster virus (VZV) (DermaQuick, Maruho, Osaka, Japan), and VZV infection was diagnosed.

cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) analysis to reveal an initial pressure of 16 cm H2O, leucocyte count of 217/μL (lymphocytes 92%), protein level of 129 mg/dL and glucose level of 55 mg/dL (blood glucose level of 138 mg/dL).
A week later, his CSF tested positive for VZV DNA via PCR.
he received intravenous acyclovir for 14 days resulting in improvement of symptoms.

accepted_aliases: meningitis caused by varicella zoster virus
diagnostic_reasoning_verbatim_spans: Hence, meningitis caused by VZV reactivation was suspected, and he received intravenous acyclovir for 14 days resulting in improvement of symptoms.
A week later, his CSF tested positive for VZV DNA via PCR.
